takeaway: Blood clotting is reversed by plasmin (fibrinolysin); platelets come from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.

question.say: With regard to blood clotting, which statement is true?

answer.say: The answer: it is reversed by plasmin, also called fibrinolysin.

lines.text: The circulation is high-pressure, so a small vessel injury can bleed fast.
lines.say: We have a high-pressure circulation, so even slight vessel damage can lead to a rapid loss of blood volume.

lines.text: The body answers with a complicated clotting response.
lines.say: To stop bleeding, the body has developed quite complicated responses to vessel damage.

lines.text: Platelets come from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.
lines.say: Blood platelets are formed from megakaryocytes in the bone marrow.

lines.text: Plasmin cuts the clot net: the clot is reversed.
lines.say: (laugh) And here comes plasmin, with golden scissors, cutting the net of the clot. The clot is reversed by plasmin, also called fibrinolysin.
Remember: plasmin, or fibrinolysin, reverses clotting.
